name: Major cyber incidents
value: DWP services offline after cyber incident
summary: UK DWP takes some online services offline after a cyber incident on 27 Nov; benefit payments unaffected
state: The UK Department for Work and Pensions said on 27 Nov it identified a cyber incident and took some online services offline as a precaution, working with the NCSC; regular benefit and pension payments are not affected (GOV.UK). ITV reported that applying for and signing in to universal credit and job search were unavailable (ITV). FinCEN systems were taken offline after an intrusion disclosed on 24 Nov. Disruption to critical services keeps Watch.
for_you: DWP says benefit and pension payments will be paid as normal; customers needing help should call their usual benefit line. Follow NCSC advice on phishing.
rubric_hit: Attack disrupting a critical government service = Watch; no national-scale attack

sources.title: GOV.UK — Temporary disruption to some DWP online services
ITV News — 'Cyber incident' affecting Department for Work and Pensions as services offline

why: Ransomware and state hacking now shut down hospitals, retailers, carmakers and airports for weeks.
drivers: Ransomware gangs, state actors, zero-days, supply-chain compromises.

rubric.alert: National-scale attack on critical infrastructure (power, health, finance), or a destructive state-attributed attack.
rubric.watch: Ransomware or attack disrupting a large company or critical service, or a mass-exploited zero-day.
rubric.normal: No major incidents disrupting critical services this week.
